# **Playlist Manager: Specification (Revised)**

Team: Krish Joshi, Kaustubh Pasumarthi, Kim Delgadillo, Colin Fahmy

**Design decisions fixed across the whole document:** LinkedChain\<T\> is **singly linked** with firstNode and numberOfEntries(no tail, no prev). Public chain methods are exactly those in Section 5\. MusicPlayer tracks position with currentIndex: int, never a node. Items marked **\[confirm\]** are things the team must verify against your actual code.

## **1\. Class Design**

| Class | Single responsibility | Collaborators |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| LinkedChain\<T\> | Generic ordered storage of non-null entries. Knows nothing about songs or playlists. | Node\<T\> (private nested) |
| Node\<T\> | Holds one entry and a link to the next node. Private to LinkedChain. | none |
| Song | Immutable data for one track, plus equality and display. | none |
| Album | A titled group of tracks loaded from the library file. | LinkedChain\<Song\> |
| Playlist | The user's ordered list of songs: add, remove, move, shuffle, read. | LinkedChain\<Song\> |
| MusicPlayer | Simulated playback state: which playlist position is current, playing or paused. | Playlist |
| InputValidator | Stateless yes/no checks on raw user input. No printing, no storage. | none |
| LibraryLoader | Reads the song-library file and builds LinkedChain\<Album\>; skips malformed lines. | Song, Album, InputValidator |
| PlaylistApp | Console menu: reads input, calls the other classes, prints results and errors. | all of the above |

**Why this split.** LinkedChain owns storage only, so it can be reused for Song and Album without change. Application rules (moving, shuffling) live in Playlist, which composes a chain rather than extending it. Playlist and Album both wrap a LinkedChain\<Song\> on purpose: an album is fixed file-order data from the library, while a playlist is user-ordered and mutable, and they expose different operations.

**Alternatives rejected.**

•      *Validation inside Playlist:* rejected because bad text input must trigger a re-prompt, which is a UI concern. Mixing it in would make Playlist print or prompt.  
•      *Merging MusicPlayer into Playlist:* rejected because playback state (playing, current position) changes independently of list contents.  
•      *Doubly linked chain with a tail:* rejected for now (see Section 4\) to keep the provided LinkedChain.java mostly intact.

## **3\. The Generic Contract**

public class LinkedChain\<T\>: **no bound** on T.

•      **Why no bound.** The app stores Song and Album, neither of which has a natural order, and the chain never sorts; the user controls order. Comparable would be wrong, and the chain only needs equals(), which every object has.  
•      **Promise about T.** Every stored entry is non-null, of type T, and found by equals().  
•      **Duplicates allowed.** No add method checks for an existing copy.  
•      **Null policy.** add, addToEnd, addAt throw IllegalArgumentException on null. remove(T), contains, count, indexOf treat null as "not found" and never throw.  
•      **Search uses equals()** and acts on the first match. Song and Album must override equals and hashCode.  
•      **Type safety.** All signatures use T or T\[\]; no raw types, no casts. A LinkedChain\<Song\> rejects an Album at compile time. toArray(T\[\] values) takes a caller-supplied array because Java cannot create new T\[n\]: chain.toArray(new Song\[chain.size()\]).  
•      **Traversal rule.** get(i) walks from the head, so a for loop calling get(i) is O(n²). To display or rebuild a list, call toArrayonce.

## **4\. Data & State**

**What backs LinkedChain\<T\>.** A singly linked chain. Fields: firstNode: Node\<T\> (null when empty) and numberOfEntries: int(updated by every add/remove, so size()/isEmpty() are O(1)). Node\<T\> is a private static nested class with data: T (never null) and next: Node\<T\> (null at the end). Outside code only ever sees T, never nodes.

**Tradeoff.** With no tail reference, addToEnd walks the chain (O(n)), so Playlist.addSong is O(n). A tail reference would make it O(1) but means keeping it correct in every remove; we accepted O(n) for simplicity.

| Class | Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| LinkedChain\<T\> | firstNode | Node\<T\> | null if empty |
|   | numberOfEntries | int | node count |
| Node\<T\> | data | T | non-null |
|   | next | Node\<T\> | null at end |
| Song | title, artist, album | String | non-blank |
|   | durationSec | int | must be \> 0 |
| Album | title, artist | String |   |
|   | tracks | LinkedChain\<Song\> | file order |
| Playlist | name | String |   |
|   | songs | LinkedChain\<Song\> | duplicates allowed, user-ordered |
| MusicPlayer | playlist | Playlist |   |
|   | currentIndex | int | \-1 \= nothing selected |
|   | playing | boolean |   |
| PlaylistApp | player | MusicPlayer |   |
|   | library | LinkedChain\<Album\> | loaded at startup |
| InputValidator | MAX\_TITLE\_LENGTH | static final int | 200; no instance state |
| LibraryLoader | none |   | stateless |

**Invariants.**

1\.     Empty chain: firstNode \== null and numberOfEntries \== 0.  
2\.     numberOfEntries equals the number of nodes reachable from firstNode.  
3\.     No node's data is null.  
4\.     MusicPlayer.currentIndex is \-1 or in \[0, playlist.size()-1\]; if the playlist is empty it is \-1 and playing is false.  
5\.     Every Song has a non-blank title, artist, album and durationSec \> 0.

## **5\. Method Signatures**

### **5.1 LinkedChain\<T\>**

Status: **given** \= from the provided LinkedChain.java; **new** \= our addition. (The earlier draft's addLast and swap are removed; nothing needs them.)

| Signature | Behavior | Time (why) | Status |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| boolean add(T newEntry) | Inserts at front. IllegalArgumentException if null. | O(1) new first node | given |
| boolean addToEnd(T newEntry) | Appends at end. IllegalArgumentException if null. | O(n) walks to last node | given |
| T remove() | Removes/returns first entry; null if empty. | O(1) | given |
| boolean remove(T anEntry) | Removes first match; false if absent or null. | O(n) search | given |
| void clear() | Removes all entries. | O(1) drop head | given |
| T get(int index) | Entry at index. IndexOutOfBoundsExceptionif out of range. | O(n) walk | given |
| boolean contains(T anEntry) | True if an entry equals it. | O(n) | given |
| int count(T anEntry) | Number of equal entries. | O(n) full scan | given |
| int size() | Entry count. | O(1) field | given |
| boolean isEmpty() | True if size is 0\. | O(1) | given |
| T\[\] toArray(T\[\] values) | Copies entries in order into values; IllegalArgumentException if null or too small. | O(n) | given |
| String toString() | "\[a, b, c\]"; "\[\]" if empty. | O(n) | given |
| void addAt(int index, T newEntry) | Inserts so entry lands at index (0 ≤ index ≤ size). IndexOutOfBoundsExceptionbad index; IllegalArgumentExceptionnull. | O(n) walk to index-1 | new |
| T removeAt(int index) | Removes/returns entry at index. IndexOutOfBoundsExceptionif out of range. | O(n) | new |
| int indexOf(T anEntry) | Index of first match; \-1 if absent or null. | O(n) | new |

Why added: Playlist.moveSong needs removeAt and addAt; LibraryLoader uses indexOf to find an existing album before adding a track. **\[confirm\]** the exact return types of the given methods match your file.

## **6\. Where Validation Lives**

Rule of thumb: **InputValidator and PlaylistApp catch user mistakes and re-prompt; Playlist, Album, Song and LinkedChainthrow exceptions as a safety net** so a bug can never corrupt the data.

| Bad input / edge case | Caught by | Response |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Blank, null, or \>200-char title | InputValidator.checkTitle (called by PlaylistApp) | Returns false; app prints "Title must be 1-200 characters" and re-prompts. Checked in the UI layer because it needs a re-prompt. |
| Index negative or ≥ size | InputValidator.checkIndex, then Playlist.moveSong/getSong | App prints "Enter a position from 0 to N-1" and re-prompts. If it still reaches Playlist, IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown and the list is unchanged. |
| Null song | InputValidator.checkSong, then Playlist.addSong / Album.addTrack | App rejects before the call; if it reaches the data layer,IllegalArgumentException. |
| Song with invalid fields (blank text, duration ≤ 0\) | Song constructor | IllegalArgumentException; the app or loader reports it and does not add the song. |
| Remove a song not in the playlist | Playlist.removeSong returns false | App prints "Song not found"; playlist unchanged. |
| Remove from empty playlist | Playlist.removeSong returns false (chain empty) | App checks size() \== 0 first and prints "Playlist is empty". |
| Play/next/previous on empty playlist | MusicPlayer returns false | App prints "Nothing to play". |
| Next on last song / previous on first | MusicPlayer.nextTrack/previousTrackreturn false | currentIndex unchanged; app prints "End/Start of playlist reached". |
| Shuffle of empty or one-song playlist | Playlist.shuffle | Silent no-op. |
| Invalid menu option | PlaylistApp.showMenu | Prints "Invalid option" and re-prompts. |
| Malformed or missing library file/line | LibraryLoader.loadLibrary | Missing file: report and return empty library. Bad line: report line number, skip it, keep loading. |
| Duplicate songs | none | Intentionally allowed. |

## **7\. Test Plan**

Fixtures: songs A, B, C, D (distinct); playlist P \= \[A, B, C\]; chain X \= \[a, b, c\].

### **LinkedChain**

| Method | Normal case → result | Bad/edge case → result |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| add | add z to X → \[z, a, b, c\], size 4 | add null → IllegalArgumentException, X unchanged |
| addToEnd | add z → \[a, b, c, z\] | add null → IllegalArgumentException |
| remove() | on X → returns a, X \= \[b, c\] | on empty chain → returns null |
| remove(T) | remove b → true, X \= \[a, c\] | remove q or null → false, unchanged |
| clear | on X → size 0 | on empty → no error |
| get | get(1) → b | get(-1) and get(3) → IndexOutOfBoundsException |
| contains | contains b → true | contains q or null → false |
| count | chain \[a, b, a\], count a → 2 | count q / null → 0 |
| size | X → 3 | empty → 0 |
| isEmpty | X → false | empty → true |
| toArray | new String\[3\] → \[a, b, c\] | null, or new String\[2\] → IllegalArgumentException |
| toString | X → "\[a, b, c\]" | empty → "\[\]" |
| addAt | addAt(1, z) → \[a, z, b, c\] | addAt(5, z) → IndexOutOfBoundsException; addAt(1, null) → IllegalArgumentException |
| removeAt | removeAt(2) → returns c, X \= \[a, b\] | removeAt(3) on X → IndexOutOfBoundsException; on empty chain → same |
| indexOf | chain \[a, b, a\], indexOf a → 0 | indexOf q or null → \-1 |

### **Application classes**

| Method | Normal case → result | Bad/edge case → result |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Song constructor | ("Espresso", "Sabrina Carpenter", "Short n' Sweet", 175\) → created | duration 0 or blank title → IllegalArgumentException |
| Song.equals | two songs with identical fields → true | compare with null or an Album→ false |
| Song.toString | the song above → "Espresso \- Sabrina Carpenter (2:55)" | title containing & and quotes → returned unchanged, no crash |
| Album.addTrack | add A → tracks \= \[A\] | add null → IllegalArgumentException, unchanged |
| Album.toString | album with 2 tracks → title, artist, "2 tracks" | album with 0 tracks → "0 tracks", no crash |
| Playlist.addSong | P add D → \[A, B, C, D\], size 4 | add null → IllegalArgumentException, size 3 |
| Playlist.removeSong | remove B → true, \[A, C\] | remove D (absent) → false; on empty playlist → false |
| Playlist.moveSong | move(0, 2\) → \[B, C, A\] | move(-1, 1\) or move(0, 3\) → IndexOutOfBoundsException, still \[A, B, C\] |
| Playlist.shuffle | P shuffled → still exactly A, B, C, size 3 | empty or one-song → unchanged, no crash |
| Playlist.getSong | getSong(2) → C | getSong(3) → IndexOutOfBoundsException (the UI normally stops this earlier via checkIndex) |
| Playlist.size | P → 3 | empty → 0 |
| MusicPlayer.play | P → true, playing true, current \= A | empty → false, playing false |
| MusicPlayer.pause | while playing → playing false | when stopped → still false |
| MusicPlayer.nextTrack | at A → true, current \= B | at C → false, still C |
| MusicPlayer.previousTrack | at B → true, current \= A | at A → false, still A |
| InputValidator.checkTitle | "Espresso" → true | "   ", null, 201 chars → false |
| InputValidator.checkIndex | (2, 5\) → true | (-1, 5), (5, 5\) → false |
| InputValidator.checkSong | valid Song → true | null → false |
| LibraryLoader.loadLibrary | file with 3 valid lines → 3 songs grouped into albums | missing file → empty library plus message; one malformed line → skipped, others loaded |
| PlaylistApp.main | normal start → menu appears | missing library file → app still starts with empty library |
| PlaylistApp.showMenu | enter valid option → action runs | enter "abc" → "Invalid option", re-prompt |

## **8\. Revised Scope**

The goal and MVP are unchanged: load songs, add and remove songs, reorder and shuffle, and play/next/previous controls.

| Change | Why | Origin |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Split the app into PlaylistApp, MusicPlayer, Playlist, Song, Album, InputValidator | Scope listed features but not who owns them; one job per class | Group discussion |
| Chose a singly linked chain (firstNode, numberOfEntries, no tail/prev) | Matches provided LinkedChain.java; simpler to keep correct | Group discussion |
| Added addAt, removeAt, indexOfto LinkedChain | moveSong needs the first two; library loading needs indexOf | Group discussion |
| Dropped addLast and swap | Redundant with addToEnd and removeAt\+addAt | GenAI review, confirmed by group |
| Decided null handling, duplicates allowed, equals()search | Needed to define the generic contract | Group discussion |
| Replaced MusicPlayer.current: Node\<Song\> with currentIndex: int | Node is private to the chain | GenAI review, confirmed by group |
| Relaxed shuffle to a uniform random order with no adjacency guarantee | Guarantee not achievable in O(n) on a linked chain | GenAI review, confirmed by group |

*(Correction from the first draft: the earlier text said we defined "head and tail references". That was wrong; there is no tail.)*

**GenAI reflection.** We gave GenAI our draft spec and the grading rubric and asked it to find missing details, contradictions between sections, and whether our generic contract was enforced by the signatures. It flagged: (1) the class table said head/tail/size/prev while Data & State said firstNode/numberOfEntries with no tail; (2) method names differed between tables (addLast, swap); (3) MusicPlayer held a private Node\<Song\>; (4) no signatures for app classes; (5) no invariants; (6) the shuffle guarantee was unrealistic; (7) the Revised Scope wrongly mentioned a tail. We reviewed each as a group, accepted all of them, and rewrote the affected sections. We verified Big-O estimates by hand and ran no code through GenAI.
